It’s telling that the Treasury’s actions last week to buy back more long-dated paper and issue more Bills took down the dollar and caused both gold and Bitcoin to soar. The market senses a slippery slope towards fiscal dominance and a possible loss in Fed independence. The assumption here is that for the Treasury to be successful in keeping yields down, it will need to significantly increase the size of the buybacks. That might require the Fed to become complicit in this operation twist, which takes us down the debasement path.  Loose fiscal policy combined with loose monetary policy is a clear negative for the dollar (which is sitting on a long term trendline), and a clear positive for gold (and by extension Bitcoin).

Lastly, we now have a market where almost all assets are moving higher.

When risky and safe haven assets rise simultaneously, you know disruption is here.

Asset owners are the only winners in this market.

Bitcoin is ripping, but many people remain sidelined.

Why?

People have been pissed off for over a year now. They are out here blaming Saylor for selling Bitcoin or thinking that BIP-110 was some existential crisis.

After prolonged periods of negativity, people become so used to the pain they forget what it's like to feel good again.

We like to think we are super logical creatures, but inside all of us is an emotional little kid who is mad that the orange coin didn't do exactly what we wanted, on exactly the timeline we predicted.

Last time I posted this I had people showing up saying that they were immune to emotions.

No dumbass. 

You're just blind to them.

You can't remove emotionality from our lives, but we can get better at navigating it and seeing when we are influenced by the tides of the crowd.

People are so traumatized after the past year that they (despite things looking incredibly positive for Bitcoin) are still in that same negative mindset.

Something shifted last week.

But sometimes our mood-based monkey minds are slow to pick up on the realities of the new world.

I think it's high time to embrace optimism again.

Ep. 202 of Facts vs Feelings stars @SecScottBessent and @Meghan_Trainor. We are all about DeBase this week. Other topics:

🏔️ The 30-year yield hit 5.33%, the highest since 2007. Treasury responded by doubling long-end buybacks starting September 9. Markets called it debasement.

🪙 Gold +5-6%, Bitcoin +20%, dollar index -1% on the week. Rising yields usually strengthen a currency. This time it went the other way.

🏦 Sonu's read: this is Operation Twist, not QE. It shifts duration without expanding the money supply, but it can still push short-term yields and imported inflation higher.

📰 Druckenmiller's WSJ op-ed argued the buybacks suppress the only fiscal disciplinarian left in Washington. Guy Berger pushed back. Ryan and Sonu debate whether the move is really that powerful.

📈 Nominal GDP growth near 5.5% versus roughly 5.8% in the late 1990s, with yields well below where they were then. Sonu thinks equilibrium sits higher than current levels, not lower.

🏭 Philly Fed 47.4, highest since 2021. Flash PMI 56, highest since April 2022. Most of the industrial strength traces to AI driven investment.

💵 $40T debt, put in context against rising household net worth.

🧭 Plus market breadth, S&P 500 support levels, portfolio diversifiers, and the setup into Jackson Hole and Nvidia.
